title: How a 22-year-old solopreneur built Morise to 3-4 lakhs/month, bootstrapped
summary: Priyam walks through building a solo AI YouTube-tools web app: spotting a gap in an AI hype wave, shipping a minimal MVP, launching on Product Hunt, and growing via SEO and build-in-public. He also covers pricing by buyer type, recurring revenue, selling a startup, and his own mistakes.

principles.text: Don't overcomplicate the build; reuse existing open-source code instead of reinventing it.
principles.quote: don't overcomplicate things. A lot of people, what they do is, they try to do something really complex. Something that already has an open-source solution.

principles.text: Keep the product narrow: minimize features and niche down so it is simple to explain.
principles.quote: I think it's very important to minimize features, niche down more, and go that way.

principles.text: SEO is his favorite acquisition channel: write content on your own domain that ranks and hooks readers to the product.
principles.quote: My favorite way to get customers is SEO

principles.text: Price by who is buying: businesses pay more than consumers, so study how your market buys first.
principles.quote: So I think first, you have to figure out how people in the market are going to buy. And price on the basis of that.

principles.text: Prefer subscriptions to one-time sales because recurring revenue keeps income flowing when you pause marketing.
principles.quote: Everyone has put a subscription on everything. So people are more used to it. And it can help you take breaks.

principles.text: Talk to your customers, especially early big names, instead of just posting about them.
principles.quote: I had like really, really big names coming in. I was just like, okay, let's put it on stories, post on Twitter, and not talk with them literally.
